title: Cloud Security Engineering Roadmap
summary: A 12-week professional immersion into cloud security architectures, IAM enforcement, container runtime defense, and automated compliance auditing.
assumptions: Assumes working fluency with Linux CLI and standard TCP/IP networking primitives.
Assumes basic cloud provider familiarity (AWS/GCP/Azure compute and storage).
Paced at 6 hours per week combining conceptual security models and hands-on laboratory exercises.

phases.title: Phase 1: Zero Trust Architecture & Identity Governance
phases.goal: Master least-privilege IAM policies, boundary enforcement, and cryptographic secrets management.

project.title: Phase 1 Milestone: Multi-Account Least-Privilege IAM Boundary Suite
project.brief: Architect and deploy a hardened AWS/GCP IAM permission boundary hierarchy with automated policy linting and break-glass temporary elevation.
acceptance_criteria: Zero wildcard (*) actions on data-tier resources
Automated CI/CD policy validation blocking overly permissive roles
MFA-enforced session token generation for administrative operations
project.stretch: Integrate automated revocation triggers based on anomaly alerts in CloudTrail.

weeks.theme: Week 1: Identity & Access Management (IAM) Deep Dive

sessions.title: IAM Policy Evaluation Logic & Permission Boundaries
sessions.objective: Understand the precise deterministic evaluation order of AWS IAM policies (explicit denies, boundaries, SCPs, and session policies).
search_queries: AWS IAM policy evaluation logic deep dive

video.title: AWS Security Specialty Course: Deep Dive into IAM Policies
video.why: Clear breakdown of policy evaluation algorithms and common evaluation pitfalls with production examples.

alternate_video.title: Mastering AWS Identity and Access Management
alternate_video.why: Official architectural overview detailing permission boundaries at enterprise scale.

checkpoints.question: When evaluating an AWS request, what occurs if both an Allow and an Explicit Deny match?
options: The Explicit Deny always overrides any Allow
The Allow overrides if placed on an inline policy
The request triggers a 409 conflict error
checkpoints.explanation: Explicit Deny always supersedes any Allow in AWS evaluation logic.

checkpoints.question: What is the primary role of a Permission Boundary on an IAM principal?
options: It grants permissions automatically to new users
It sets the maximum possible permissions an entity can be granted
It replaces the need for resource-based policies
checkpoints.explanation: Permission boundaries set the outer limit of allowable permissions without granting rights on their own.

checkpoints.question: Hands-on Verification: Test IAM Evaluation Order
options: Simulated policy evaluation via CLI/Console confirming explicit deny precedence
Skipped simulation due to credential setup
Created an unrestricted admin policy to test connectivity
checkpoints.taskCriteria: Run AWS IAM policy simulator or terraform policy test confirming boundary limits.
checkpoints.explanation: Testing with simulation tools proves least-privilege boundary boundaries hold.

sessions.title: Secrets Management & Cryptographic Key Rings
sessions.objective: Design automated key rotation, envelope encryption with KMS, and dynamic database credentials injection.

video.title: Cloud Cryptography & Envelope Encryption Explained
video.why: Visual explanation of customer master keys, data keys, and the mathematical mechanics of envelope encryption.

alternate_video.title: Cloud Key Management Deep Dive
alternate_video.why: Comprehensive walkthrough of hardware security modules (HSMs) and cloud key ring hierarchies.

checkpoints.question: Why is envelope encryption preferred over direct KMS encryption for large payloads?
options: KMS API enforces a 4KB plaintext limit and network round-trips for large data degrade throughput
KMS does not support symmetric keys
Plaintext data must never be decrypted
Envelope encryption eliminates key rotation requirements
checkpoints.explanation: KMS encrypts the data encryption key (DEK) locally, avoiding round-trips of bulk data over the API.

weeks.theme: Week 2: Cloud Network Segmentation & Perimeter Defense

sessions.title: VPC Peering, Transit Gateways & PrivateLink Architecture
sessions.objective: Isolate microservices into dedicated subnets and route internal traffic without internet gateway exposure.
search_queries: AWS VPC peering transit gateway architecture

video.title: AWS Networking Masterclass: VPCs, Subnets & Transit Gateways
video.why: Hands-on walkthrough of secure subnet topology, route tables, and VPC endpoints.

phases.title: Phase 2: Container & Kubernetes Security Hardening
phases.goal: Implement immutable container supply chains, vulnerability scanning, and eBPF runtime observability.

project.title: Phase 2 Milestone: Hardened Kubernetes Cluster with Admission Control
project.brief: Deploy an Amazon EKS / GKE cluster with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper enforcing non-root execution and cosign signature verification.
acceptance_criteria: All pods blocked if running as root user (UID 0)
Unsigned container images rejected at admission webhook
project.stretch: Deploy Cilium with eBPF-based L7 network monitoring and automated anomalous egress drops.

weeks.theme: Week 3: Container Image Security & Supply Chain Defense

sessions.title: SLSA Framework, SBOM Generation & Image Signing with Cosign
sessions.objective: Build a reproducible container pipeline generating SPDX SBOMs and cryptographic attestations.

video.title: Container Security: Scanning, Signing & Verification
video.why: Covers automated scanning in CI/CD, signing with Cosign, and verifying in Kubernetes.
